title: BEFORE I WAS BORN.
body: The last note is in a different hand — older, formal, the pen pressed hard: my father trained under the night operator. my father is sixty-two. the night operator looks thirty. ask him what he eats. — P. Someone has written underneath, in the first hand, smaller: don't. i already asked. The note is not dated. The paper has the soft, worn feel of a page that has been folded for decades and only now left out where a night operator could find it.

choices.label: Copy both notes into your logbook.

outcome.text: You copy them word for word, including the correction. The logbook is the only record the city cannot revise. When you look up, the board is clean — the notes are gone, and you do not remember them being taken, and the coffee is warm, and the clock says 01:00, and the logbook does not forget.

choices.label: Tear them down. They are wrong about you.

outcome.text: You tear them down. The shreds go in the bin; the bin is empty by morning. They are wrong about you — you are thirty, you are not thirty, you do not remember being hired. The day crew will write new notes about the night operator who reads the board.
